title: Remember Your Roots
summary: The Lord calls those who seek righteousness to remember the rock from which they were hewn and to look to Abraham and Sarah, whom he called and blessed.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord addresses those who follow righteousness and tells them to look to the rock and pit from which they were hewn.
The Lord tells them to look to Abraham and Sarah, saying he called Abraham alone and blessed him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The speech can be presented as off-screen narration over an unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether anyone is visibly present to hear the address.
The appearance of the rock and pit as metaphors.

narration.text: Hearken unto me, ye that follow after righteousness.
Look unto Abraham, your father, and unto Sarah, she that bare you;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The rock and pit are figurative language, not described visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal pit or rock as the origin of the addressed people.
Do not invent an appearance for the Lord.

title: Zion Comforted
summary: The Lord promises comfort for Zion and describes her waste places becoming like Eden and a garden, with joy, gladness, thanksgiving, and melody.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says he will comfort Zion and her waste places, making the wilderness like Eden and the desert like the garden of the Lord; joy, gladness, thanksgiving, and melody will be there.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The teaching may be voiced off-screen over a barren landscape; the promised transformation is not narrated as occurring now.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of Zion, Eden, or the garden.
Whether any people are visible.

narration.text: For the Lord shall comfort Zion, he will comfort all her waste places;
Joy and gladness shall be found therein, thanksgiving and the voice of melody.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The promised likeness to Eden is figurative or prospective, not a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the promised transformation as happening in the present.

title: A Light for the People
summary: The Lord calls his people and nation to listen, promising that his law will proceed from him and his judgment will be a light; he declares his righteousness and salvation near.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord calls his people and nation to listen, saying a law will proceed from him and his judgment will be a light for the people.
The Lord says his righteousness is near, his salvation has gone forth, and his arm will judge the people; the isles will wait upon and trust in him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The address can be shown as off-screen speech over an unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: Who, if anyone, is visibly listening.
Any literal form for the Lord's arm or judgment.

narration.text: Hearken unto me, my people; and give ear unto me, O my nation;
My righteousness is near; my salvation is gone forth,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord's arm and judgment are expressions of power and justice, not described visible forms.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal arm or supernatural manifestation not described in the text.

title: Salvation Endures
summary: The Lord contrasts the heavens and earth passing away and their inhabitants dying with his salvation lasting forever and his righteousness not being abolished.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says the heavens will vanish like smoke, the earth will grow old like a garment, and its inhabitants will die; his salvation will be forever and his righteousness will not be abolished.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The teaching may be voiced off-screen over a view of the heavens and earth.
unspecified_visual_details: Any visual depiction of the heavens vanishing or the earth aging.
Whether anyone is visible.

narration.text: Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look upon the earth beneath;
But my salvation shall be forever, and my righteousness shall not be abolished.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse states a comparison and future condition; it does not narrate the heavens vanishing as a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the earth or heavens literally deteriorating in this moment.

title: Do Not Fear Reproach
summary: The Lord tells those who know righteousness not to fear the reproach of men, whose fate is compared to a garment eaten by moths and worms, while his righteousness and salvation endure.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord tells those who know righteousness and have his law in their hearts not to fear men's reproach or revilings.
The Lord compares men's fate to garments and wool eaten by moths and worms, and says his righteousness and salvation endure through generations.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The teaching can be presented as off-screen speech without depicting the comparisons literally.
unspecified_visual_details: Who is addressed or visibly present.
Any literal garment or insect imagery.

narration.text: fear ye not the reproach of men, neither be ye afraid of their revilings.
But my righteousness shall be forever, and my salvation from generation to generation.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The moth and worm comparison is figurative teaching.
prohibited_inventions: Do not literalize the garment and wool comparison as an event.

title: Remember the Lord's Power
summary: The speaker calls on the arm of the Lord to awaken and recalls the Lord cutting Rahab, wounding the dragon, drying the sea, and making a way through its depths for the ransomed.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker calls on the arm of the Lord to awake as in ancient days and asks whether it cut Rahab and wounded the dragon.
The speaker recalls the Lord drying the sea and making a way through its depths for the ransomed to pass over.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The prayer can be shown as off-screen speech over an unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of Rahab or the dragon.
Whether the sea-crossing is to be depicted; no participants or visual particulars are supplied here.

narration.text: Awake, awake! Put on strength, O arm of the Lord;
that hath made the depths of the sea a way for the ransomed to pass over?

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The arm is figurative; the verses recall past acts rather than narrating them as a present scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a visible appearance for the Lord, Rahab, or the dragon.
Do not stage the recalled events as occurring now.

title: The Redeemed Return
summary: The redeemed of the Lord are described as returning to Zion with singing and everlasting joy, while sorrow and mourning flee away.

explicit_facts.text: The redeemed of the Lord shall return and come with singing to Zion; everlasting joy and holiness shall be upon them, and sorrow and mourning shall flee away.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A future return with singing is described, but the verse supplies no specific participants or visual details.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity and appearance of the redeemed.
The route, time, and visual appearance of Zion.

narration.text: Therefore, the redeemed of the Lord shall return, and come with singing unto Zion;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a promised future event, not a present return.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent identities or appearances for the redeemed.

title: Comfort and Fear
summary: “I am he; yea, I am he that comforteth you.” “And where is the fury of the oppressor?”

explicit_facts.text: The speaker identifies himself as the one who comforts the addressee and questions fear of mortal man.
The speech identifies the Lord as the addressee’s maker, who stretched forth the heavens and laid the earth’s foundations.
The speaker questions forgetting the Lord and continually fearing the oppressor’s fury as though destruction were imminent.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The speech can be presented without a visible speaker or a specific physical setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The addressee’s identity and appearance.
The oppressor’s identity and appearance.
The physical setting; no divine appearance is described.

spoken_dialogue.text: I am he; yea, I am he that comforteth you. Behold, who art thou, that thou shouldst be afraid of man, who shall die, and of the son of man, who shall be made like unto grass?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: And where is the fury of the oppressor?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Creation is recalled in speech, not narrated as a present event.
The comparison to grass is figurative, not a visible transformation.
The oppressor’s anticipated destruction is not narrated as an actual attack.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an unstated visible appearance of the Lord.
Do not stage creation, an oppressor’s attack, or a person transforming into grass.
Do not invent an audience, setting, or additional dialogue.

title: Assurance to the Captive Exile
summary: The captive exile hasteneth, that he may be loosed, and that he should not die in the pit, nor that his bread should fail. But I am the Lord thy God, whose waves roared; the Lord of Hosts is my name.

explicit_facts.text: The captive exile hastens so that he may be loosed, not die in the pit, and not have his bread fail.
The Lord identifies himself as the Lord thy God and the Lord of Hosts, whose waves roared.
The Lord says he has put his words in the addressee's mouth and covered the addressee in the shadow of his hand.
The Lord states the purpose of planting the heavens, laying the foundations of the earth, and saying to Zion that Zion is his people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A nonrepresentational presentation can accompany the words without staging reported events or depicting divine appearance.
unspecified_visual_details: Background, typography, and composition.
The exile's appearance and physical surroundings.
The identity of the addressee designated by 'thy' and 'thee'.

spoken_dialogue.text: But I am the Lord thy God, whose waves roared; the Lord of Hosts is my name.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

narration.text: The captive exile hasteneth, that he may be loosed, and that he should not die in the pit, nor that his bread should fail.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The exile's release, survival, and continued bread are aims, not narrated outcomes.
The final dialogue excerpt is embedded in the Lord's stated purpose of speaking to Zion, not a separately staged encounter.
The hand, heavens, and foundations language does not establish a visible supernatural event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the reported exile's hastening as a new present-tense event.
Do not depict release, death, starvation, or arrival at a destination.
Do not invent a visible appearance of the Lord or a literal divine hand.
Do not stage roaring waves, creation, or words physically entering a mouth.
Do not invent an identity for the addressee or place mentioned figures together physically.

title: Jerusalem Is Called to Rise
summary: Jerusalem is called to awake and stand after drinking the cup of the Lord's fury; no son among those she bore or raised is described as guiding or taking her by the hand.

explicit_facts.text: Jerusalem is called to awake and stand after drinking the cup of the Lord's fury and its dregs.
None of Jerusalem's sons is described as guiding her or taking her by the hand.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The address may be voiced off-screen over a view of Jerusalem.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether Jerusalem is represented as a person or a city.
The identity and appearance of her sons.

narration.text: Awake, awake, stand up, O Jerusalem,
And none to guide her among all the sons she hath brought forth;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The cup of fury and Jerusalem's drinking are figurative language.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict literal drinking or assign an unprovided identity to Jerusalem's sons.

title: Two Sons Remain
summary: Two sons come to Jerusalem to grieve over her desolation, destruction, famine, and sword. Her other sons have fainted, while the two lie at the head of the streets like a wild bull in a net.

explicit_facts.text: Two sons come to Jerusalem and are sorry for her desolation, destruction, famine, and sword.
Jerusalem's sons have fainted except for the two; the two lie at the head of all the streets, compared to a wild bull in a net.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The two sons are visible lying at the head of a street.
unspecified_visual_details: The sons' identities, ages, and appearance.
The cause and appearance of their fainting.

narration.text: These two sons are come unto thee, who shall be sorry for thee—
they lie at the head of all the streets;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The wild bull in a net is a comparison, not a literal animal in the scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the two sons or depict a literal bull.

title: The Cup Is Taken Away
summary: The Lord addresses afflicted Jerusalem and says he has taken the cup of trembling from her hand, so she will not drink it again.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord addresses the afflicted, described as drunken but not with wine.
The Lord says he pleads the cause of his people and has taken the cup of trembling from Jerusalem; she will not drink it again.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The speech may be voiced off-screen over Jerusalem.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether Jerusalem is personified visually.
Any literal cup or visible divine figure.

narration.text: Therefore hear now this, thou afflicted, and drunken, and not with wine:
thou shalt no more drink it again.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Drunkenness and the cup are figurative descriptions.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict literal drunkenness or invent a visible Lord.

title: The Afflicters' Words
summary: The Lord promises to put an unspecified thing into the hand of those who afflict the addressee. He recounts their demand to bow down and describes the addressee's body as ground and street to those who went over.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker promises to put what is called “it” into the hand of those who afflict the addressee.
The afflicters previously demanded that the addressee bow down so they could go over.
The addressee's body is described as having been laid as the ground and street to those who went over.

unspecified_visual_details: The identity and appearance of the addressee and afflicters.
What “it” refers to.
The physical setting.

spoken_dialogue.text: But I will put it into the hand of them that afflict thee; who have said to thy soul: Bow down, that we may go over—and thou hast laid thy body as the ground and as the street to them that went over.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord is the continuing speaker, rather than Nephi.
The afflicters' demand is embedded reported speech, not a present encounter.
The promised transfer is not narrated as completed.
The ground-and-street comparison does not establish a literal transformation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a visible appearance for the Lord.
Do not stage the reported affliction as a new present-tense event.
Do not identify the unspecified object, addressee, or afflicters.
Do not depict the promised transfer as completed or the body as literally transformed into ground or street.

title: Zion Called to Rise
summary: Zion and Jerusalem are called to awake, put on strength and beautiful garments, shake off the dust, arise, sit down, and free themselves from the bands of the captive daughter's neck.

explicit_facts.text: Zion is told to awake and put on strength; Jerusalem is told to put on beautiful garments, with no more uncircumcised or unclean entering.
Jerusalem is told to shake off dust, arise, sit down, and loose the bands from the captive daughter's neck.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The calls to rise and free herself may be presented as address rather than a depicted completed action.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether Jerusalem is a visible person, city, or both.
The appearance of the garments, dust, or bands.

narration.text: Awake, awake, put on thy strength, O Zion;
Shake thyself from the dust; arise, sit down, O Jerusalem;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Zion and Jerusalem are addressed poetically; the text does not establish a literal figure.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a visible personification or show the promised purification as a completed event.
